extracted.intended_audience: Applicants for NIAID / NIH Research Career Development (K) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, program-specific instructions and evaluative criteria for preparing and submitting NIAID/NIH Research Career Development (K) award applications, including mentored Ks. Covers peer-review considerations, career development and research plan expectations, mentor/institution responsibilities, submission, and post-award reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow NOFO and SF 424 supplemental instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read the relevant notice of funding opportunity (NOFO). Follow the supplemental instructions for K applications in the SF 424 Application Guide, including guidelines for page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check NOFO-specific elements; adhere to page limits and other SF 424 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID iD requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have an ORCID iD and associate it with their eRA Commons Personal Profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and associate ORCID before submission per eRA instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review focuses on CV, research and career plans, and reference letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers will assess your potential based on your curriculum vitae (CV), research and career plans, and (except for K24) reference letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure these documents clearly demonstrate past accomplishments and future potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: CV should highlight past successes
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your CV highlights your past successes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize publications, leadership roles, major contributions, and other evidence of productivity and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and career plans must show commitment and potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research and career plans should illustrate your commitment and potential for future contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly connect activities and milestones to long-term independent research goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters from people familiar with your qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reference letters should come from people who are familiar with your qualifications, training, and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide referees with context so letters are specific and informative; reviewers scrutinize these letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor/co-mentor letters do not count as reference letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Your mentor and any co-mentor(s) do not submit a reference letter or letter of recommendation. Instead, they add their input in other sections of the application. If a mentor or co-mentor submits a reference letter, it will not count toward your required total of three to five reference letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on mentor-submitted reference letters to meet required counts; include mentor input in designated mentor statement sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor letter of support in some Ks for portability of research
rubrics_metrics.description: For some K programs, your mentor does submit a letter of support to indicate willingness for you to take with you the portion of the research you are currently conducting in the mentor's lab to establish your own independent research career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check NOFO requirements for whether such a mentor support/portability letter is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will evaluate the institution where you conduct your proposed research. They'll consider whether the institution has suitable facilities and is committed to your development as an investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain a strong institutional letter that details time allocation, resources, and support for career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor's record and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: For mentored positions, reviewers will assess your mentor's career and research supervision record, and whether his or her work and experience are relevant to your proposed Research Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select mentors whose track records and expertise clearly align with the candidate's project and training needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for NOFO-specific peer review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Your chosen NOFO may have opportunity-specific peer review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NOFO and NIH reviewer information (e.g., 'Information for Reviewers', 'Review Criteria at a Glance') for any additional criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify need for a K award and link to independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify your need for a K award and explain how it will be a vital step toward your ultimate career goal and move you toward scientific research independence (e.g., as an R01 investigator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a persuasive case that the award bridges to independence; show explicit milestones and how K-specific support is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development plan equals Research Plan importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your career development plan is as important as your Research Plan, so spend a lot of time and effort when you develop it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed training activities, timelines, and evaluation of progress; reviewers weigh this heavily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify training, courses, consultants and frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify training and courses that you will participate in, how often you'll meet with consultants, and how all of this will help you reach your objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a realistic schedule/timeline and describe learning outcomes and how each activity fills capability gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align training emphasis to award type
rubrics_metrics.description: Stress your commitment to a career in biomedical or behavioral research (for a K08, K22, and K99/R00), patient-oriented research (K23 and K24), clinical or translational research (physician-scientist K99/R00 where at least one Specific Aim must be in this area), or integration of biomedicine and quantitative science (K25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor career development language to the expectations and emphasis of the specific K mechanism you are applying to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan appropriateness to experience level
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will evaluate whether [the Research Plan] is appropriate for and tailored to your experience level and if it allows you to develop the skills and knowledge needed for further career advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale aims and methods to be ambitious but feasible given the candidate's stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan must demonstrate innovation and acknowledge limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Research Plan needs to demonstrate innovation, address potential limitations, and indicate the skills you will gain during the course of your research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contingency plans, limitations discussion, and explicit description of skill acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate proposed research to career goals and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate the proposed research to your scientific career goals and explain how you will achieve your objectives in the time you request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide milestones and timelines linking research activities to career development outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Public Access and citation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the NIH Public Access Policy, you must list PubMed Central (PMC) identification numbers when citing a peer-reviewed journal article you have authored or coauthored and that resulted from an NIH-funded award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PMC IDs are included for applicable publications; consult Public Access SOP for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography requirements on Form Page 2
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Bibliography and References Cited section of the Research Plan, provide a bibliography of any references cited in the Project Summary and Relevance section on Form Page 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure references cited on Form Page 2 appear in the Research Plan bibliography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) instruction plan is mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: You must document training on Responsible Conduct of Research. Make sure you include a plan for instruction. If you fail to include one, your application will be considered incomplete and won't be reviewed until you provide an acceptable plan of instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Responsible Conduct of Research—Training SOP; do not rely on older sample applications for current requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address rigor and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure to address rigor and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH guidance (Enhancing Reproducibility Through Rigor and Transparency) on study design, biological variables, authentication, and statistical practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with Research With Special Considerations requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH and NIAID have special requirements for Research With Special Considerations such as human subjects, clinical research, vertebrate animals, and select agents. You may also need to Create a Resource Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and address all applicable special considerations early; include required approvals and resource sharing statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a strong, relevant mentoring team
rubrics_metrics.description: Should you need or want a mentoring team, i.e., mentor and co-mentors, find people who have expertise in your area of research. For multidisciplinary research, make sure your team covers all the scientific bases. Peer reviewers will check to see that your mentors' work and experience are relevant to your project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose mentors to cover methodological, topical, and career-development needs; document each mentor's role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentors must be accessible and demonstrate time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick mentors who are accessible. If anyone you're considering as a mentor is away often or too busy, move on to someone else. Make it crystal clear in your application that your mentors have enough time to devote to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe meeting frequency and time allocation; for off-site mentors, describe communication plans and demonstrate commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight mentors' funding and active research
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out that your mentors are active, funded investigators to show peer reviewers that they are conducting original research—research that complements yours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document mentors' current grant support and how K funds will supplement—not substitute—the mentor's funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Research Plan to generate preliminary data for future R01s
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a solid Research Plan. Don't skimp on the Research Plan thinking that because you're writing a K (not an R01) application, reviewers might be more lenient. They won't be. Ask important research questions and use the Research Plan as a vehicle to get preliminary data for a future R01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments/aims that yield publishable preliminary results and advance toward independent funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe career development activities that lead to independence and provide timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Accentuate activities. Describe how career development or training activities will lead to your independence and state how your future research will be independent from your mentors' work. We strongly recommend that you provide a career development timeline, including plans to apply for subsequent independent Research Projects (e.g., R01) grant support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit statements and timeline showing progression to independence and differentiation from mentor's research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain strong reference and institutional letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Get good reference and institutional letters. Since reviewers will scrutinize reference letters, be sure to ask people who are familiar with your qualifications, training, and interests. You should also get a strong letter from your institution that speaks to its commitment to your development into a productive, independent investigator. Officials must agree to provide adequate time and support to you for the period of the K award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide letter writers with specific points to address; institutional letters should explicitly commit protected time and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor statements must convey wholehearted support and specific contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain strong mentor statements. Be sure your mentor statements convey your mentors' wholehearted support of you. Each mentor must explain how he or she will contribute to the development of your research career and discuss the research as well as other activities, e.g., seminars and presentations at scientific meetings. Mentor statements from those who aren't at your institution should also describe their commitment to you and how frequently you will communicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid terse, non-committal language—example provided where a terse mentor letter was interpreted as lack of interest; have mentors explicitly describe time, activities, and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate productivity or explain lack thereof
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate productivity. Reviewers look closely at your productivity, e.g., number of publications, first or last author. If you're lacking in this area, explain your role on other projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain circumstances (e.g., involvement in trials that delay publications) or alternative evidence of leadership and contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify sample size and analytic plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify sample size. Explain why you are studying, for instance, 50 samples and why those in particular if they are a subset of a larger study. Get input from a biostatistician if this isn't your strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide statistical rationale, power calculations, and subgroup selection justification; consult biostatistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects section must reflect the candidate's K-funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: Address human subjects. Avoid this common mistake: completing the human subjects research section using the description from a mentor's grant application. That description may not apply to what you'll be doing with your K award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Human Subjects section from the perspective of the specific research you are conducting under the K award; include letters of permission for sample use or substudies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep RCR plans current and specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Get up-to-date on Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR). Do you know what your plan for instruction in RCR should cover? Don't rely on sample applications or information from previous K awardees that might not reflect the latest RCR requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Responsible Conduct of Research—Training SOP for current content and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have mentors review the application before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Get mentors to review your application. We highly recommend that you have your mentors (especially your primary mentor) give your application a once-over to check for thoroughness, consistency, and effective presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involve mentors in edits to avoid reviewer impressions of lack of mentor involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit electronically and check internal deadlines and due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your application electronically using the NIH Application Submission System and Interface for Submission Tracking (ASSIST) or another one of the NIH Submission Options. Check with your business office to see which approach it uses and to check their internal deadline. For most K NOFOs, AIDS and non-AIDS applications have different due dates. Check the NOFO and the Standard Due Dates for Competing Applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with institutional grants office; verify correct submission system and appropriate due date (AIDS/non-AIDS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted post-submission materials and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: You may send certain materials after you submit your application and before initial peer review. For career development awards, this includes a summary to update your sponsor's funding information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIAID's Guidelines for Sending Post-Submission Materials and NIH FAQs for specifics and allowable content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual RPPR and reporting content
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit an annual Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) each year to continue NIH support. Describe your research activities over the past reporting period. Describe training and courses along with other activities that enhanced your research skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include progress toward milestones, training activities, publications, and plans for the next year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update biosketches and other support when changes occur
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the guidelines for your award to determine if you should complete biographical sketches for new key personnel and other significant contributors. Include other support for the K award recipient, mentors, co-sponsors, and key personnel only if the support has changed since the previous submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep biosketches and Other Support current per award-specific reporting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Mentor's Report for mentored K progress reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a mentored K award—K01, K08, K23, K25, or K99—include a Mentor's Report. Mentor comments help program officers determine whether NIAID should continue funding. Give your mentors plenty of time to write feedback on your performance, and make sure they sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule mentor input well before RPPR deadlines to ensure timely, signed reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and complete reporting to avoid award delays
rubrics_metrics.description: We need your progress reports on time. Sending a late or incomplete report could delay your award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to reporting calendar and institutional procedures to avoid interruptions in funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout and audit recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: When your award ends, you'll need to file Final Reports for Grant Closeout and maintain records so you can Meet Your Audit Requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain documentation and fulfill closeout obligations as specified in award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek NIAID pre-submission eligibility and alignment advice
rubrics_metrics.description: NIAID can advise you on your eligibility for a particular K program and whether your proposed research aligns with NIAID if you send an NIH-formatted biosketch and Specific Aims page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIAID resources or contact the AI Training Help Desk for program alignment and eligibility feedback prior to submission.
